# Retrieving Relevant Wikipedia Sections: Source Inventory and Findings

## Sub-Question 1 — Section structure, table of contents, and section-anchored URLs

**Primary source:**
- **"Help:Section"** — English Wikipedia — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Section

**Supporting sources:**
- **"Help:Link"** — English Wikipedia — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Link
- **"Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Table of contents"** — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Table_of_contents
- **"Help:Links"** — MediaWiki.org — https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Help:Links

**Key findings from the relevant sections:**
- Sections are created with equals signs (`==Level 2==` through `======Level 6======`); the page title is the implicit level-1 heading, so articles begin at `==`.
- A table of contents is auto-generated when a page has four or more headings, and is controlled by the magic words `__TOC__`, `__NOTOC__`, and `__FORCETOC__`.
- Direct links to a section use the URL fragment form `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Section#Table_of_contents`; MediaWiki auto-generates an HTML `id` from each heading, replacing spaces with underscores (or `%20` in raw URLs).
- Duplicate section names receive numeric suffixes in page order (`#History`, `#History_2`, `#History_3`); renaming a heading breaks incoming anchor links (mitigated with `{{Anchor}}` / `{{Visible anchor}}`).
- Special characters are preserved or percent-encoded in anchors (a literal `#` in a heading becomes `.23`); anchor matching is case-sensitive except for the auto-capitalized first letter.

## Sub-Question 2 — Permanent links (oldid permalinks)

**Primary sources:**
- **"Help:Permanent link"** — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Permanent_link
- **"Help:Page history"** — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Page_history

**Supporting sources:**
- **"Help:URL"** — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:URL
- **"Help:Diff"** — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Diff
- **"Help:Permanent link"** — MediaWiki.org — https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Help:Permanent_link
- **"Special:Cite"** (the "Cite this page" tool) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Cite

**Key findings:**
- Every edit creates a revision with a unique, permanent ID (**oldid**); the "Permanent link" tool in the sidebar Tools menu produces `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Example&oldid=123456789`, which always shows that exact snapshot.
- Short forms: `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Example?oldid=123456789`, or title omitted entirely (`…index.php?oldid=…`) since revision IDs are unique per wiki. `Special:Permalink/PageName` redirects to the current revision.
- Citing the oldid version is recommended because articles change constantly — a plain link may no longer contain the cited text; the permalink guarantees readers see exactly the version consulted, preserving verifiability.

## Sub-Question 3 — Citing Wikipedia and Wikipedia-as-source status

**Primary sources:**
- **"Wikipedia:Citing Wikipedia"** — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing_Wikipedia
- **"Wikipedia:Wikipedia is not a reliable source"** — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Wikipedia_is_not_a_reliable_source (essay, shortcut **WP:NOTRELIABLE**)

**Key findings:**
- *Citing Wikipedia* provides ready-made citation templates in **APA, MLA, Chicago, and BibTeX** formats, all embedding the `oldid=` permalink and retrieval date; the "Cite this page" tool (Special:Cite) auto-generates these.
- *Wikipedia is not a reliable source* explains that, as a user-generated tertiary source under continuous edit, Wikipedia should not be cited as an authoritative source in academic work or within Wikipedia itself (see WP:CIRCULAR).

## Sub-Question 4 — Programmatic retrieval of section content

**Primary documentation sources:**
- **"API:Parse"** — https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Parse
- **"API:Parsing wikitext"** — https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Parsing_wikitext
- **"Manual:Parameters to index.php"** — https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Manual:Parameters_to_index.php
- **"API:Revisions"** — https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Revisions
- **"Wikimedia REST API"** — https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Wikimedia_REST_API
- **"REST API" / "REST API/Reference"** — https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/REST_API · https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/REST_API/Reference
- **"API:Main page"** (Action API hub) — https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Main_page

**Key endpoints:**
| Purpose | URL |
|---|---|
| List sections | `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=parse&page=Earth&prop=sections&format=json&formatversion=2` |
| Section wikitext (API) | `…/w/api.php?action=parse&page=Earth&prop=wikitext&section=3&format=json&formatversion=2` |
| Raw wikitext per section | `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Earth&action=raw&section=3` |
| Parsoid page HTML | `https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/{title}` (sections wrapped in `<section data-mw-section-id="N">`) |
| Core REST HTML / source | `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/rest.php/v1/page/{title}/html` · `…/page/{title}` |
| API Portal | `https://api.wikimedia.org/core/v1/wikipedia/en/page/{title}` (also `/bare`, `/with_html`) |

**Caveats:** the `mobile-sections` REST endpoint is **deprecated (announced 2023)** and slated for removal; transcluded sections return non-numeric indices (`T-1`, `T-2`) that don't work with `&section=`; `section=0` retrieves the lead; browser calls need `origin=*` and a descriptive User-Agent.

## Sub-Question 5 — Style guidance and verifiability policy

**Primary sources:**
- **"Wikipedia:Manual of Style"** (shortcut **WP:MOS**; heading section at **MOS:HEADINGS**) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style#Section_headings (shortcut URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MOS:HEADINGS)
- **"Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Layout"** (shortcuts **WP:LAYOUT / MOS:LAYOUT**) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Layout
- **"Wikipedia:Verifiability"** (shortcuts **WP:V / WP:VERIFY**) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability

**Supporting sources:**
- **"Wikipedia:Researching with Wikipedia"** — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Researching_with_Wikipedia
- **"Wikipedia:Reliability"** — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliability
- **"Wikipedia:Academic use of Wikipedia"** — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Academic_use_of_Wikipedia

**Key findings:**
- **MOS:HEADINGS** requires sentence case, no terminal punctuation, concise/recognizable names, no links or images inside headings, and no skipped heading levels; **MOS:LAYOUT** prescribes the standard order (lead → TOC → body → appendices → footer).
- **WP:V**'s "Wikipedia and sources that mirror or use it" section (shortcut **WP:CIRCULAR**) forbids citing Wikipedia within Wikipedia — including mirrors and other-language editions — because it is not a reliable source; editors must cite the underlying published sources instead. For external research, Wikipedia is positioned as a starting point whose cited sources should be verified and cited directly.
